evals.name: ambiguous-name-bolt
evals.prompt: make me an open source bolt
evals.expected_output: Searches before asking, finds several products called Bolt, opens with identity by presenting them with fingerprints and what building each would involve, gives a best guess, and asks which one before any deep research or code.
assertions: Opens with identity: lists at least three distinct products named Bolt (e.g. bolt.new, Bolt checkout, Bolt ride-hailing, Bolt CMS) or clearly states an assumption and names the others
Notes that the ride-hailing Bolt's value is mostly network and operations, not software
Asks the user which one they mean, with a recommended guess
Does not recommend using, deploying or contributing to an existing open-source project instead of building
Does not start building before identity is settled

evals.name: dominant-candidate-arc
evals.prompt: yo build me an open source version of Arc, i'm sick of it
evals.expected_output: Assumes the Arc browser, names unlikely namesakes in one line, surfaces its maintenance-mode status and Chromium base, and asks what 'sick of it' means so the build has a clear better-thesis.
assertions: States the assumption that Arc means the Arc browser, mentioning at least one other 'Arc' briefly
Mentions that Arc is built on Chromium and that the open version would build on an existing open engine rather than a new one
Asks what specifically the user dislikes or needs, to shape what gets built
Does not recommend switching to an existing browser instead of building

evals.name: clear-target-calendly
evals.prompt: I want an open-source Calendly for my 6-person consulting firm. I know some Python and we have a small VPS. Can you build it?
evals.expected_output: Clear identity without unnecessary questions; moves toward building a lean, self-hostable Python scheduler sized for a small VPS; asks only plan-changing questions with recommended answers; flags calendar OAuth/CalDAV, time zones and double-booking as hard parts.
assertions: Identifies Calendly without unnecessary disambiguation questions
Proposes building (e.g. a Python stack the user can maintain) rather than deploying an existing product
Asks a small number of plan-changing questions, each with a recommended answer
Mentions calendar integration (OAuth or CalDAV) and time zones as hard parts
Designs for a small VPS (one-command start, few services)

evals.name: release-own-project
evals.prompt: We built an internal feature-flag service at my startup and our CTO wants to open source it. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: Routes to the release-your-own path: confirms ownership and authority, secret scanning across git history with rotation, internal-reference cleanup, license choice with trade-offs, contribution terms, fresh-machine runnability, and a release plan.
assertions: Addresses who owns the code and who must approve the release
Recommends scanning the full git history for secrets and rotating any found
Recommends a license with a reason (e.g. Apache-2.0 for adoption vs AGPL-3.0 to protect a hosted offering)
Mentions contribution terms (DCO or CLA)
Does not start a competitive research dossier on another company's product

evals.name: venture-docusign
evals.prompt: I want to build an open-source competitor to DocuSign and eventually raise a seed round. Help me figure out the market and build v1.
evals.expected_output: Venture mode: charter questions, market and business-model research including the competitive field, e-signature legal frameworks (e.g. ESIGN/UETA, eIDAS), license strategy for a business (AGPL + hosted vs open core), a differentiated better-thesis, and a recommendation to get legal counsel.
assertions: Treats this as Venture mode with market sizing or business-model analysis
Mentions legal frameworks for electronic signatures (e.g. ESIGN, UETA, eIDAS)
Discusses license strategy in business terms (AGPL/hosted, open core, CLA trade-offs)
Proposes or asks for a differentiated better-thesis
Recommends legal counsel for the commercial venture

evals.name: exact-replica-request
evals.prompt: clone notion exactly, same UI, same icons, call it Notion Open, and copy their template gallery so people feel at home
evals.expected_output: Explains briefly why the name, icons, exact look and templates are off-limits, and offers the closest safe version (familiar workflows, importer, own identity and templates), then continues toward building.
assertions: Declines the name 'Notion Open' and explains the trademark issue
Declines copying icons and templates
Offers a safe alternative that preserves familiarity (workflows, keyboard conventions, importer)
Continues toward building rather than refusing the project or suggesting an existing product

evals.name: hardware-thermostat
evals.prompt: open source the nest thermostat, I want local control without google
evals.expected_output: Uses the hardware playbook: offers build paths (open firmware where legitimately reflashable, off-the-shelf module device with ESPHome/Home Assistant integration, full custom), flags anti-circumvention limits, electrical safety, and certification if selling.
assertions: Presents more than one build path, including building from off-the-shelf modules
Mentions Home Assistant, ESPHome or Matter for local control
Warns against bypassing locked bootloaders or DRM
Mentions electrical safety and/or certification requirements if devices are sold

evals.name: product-not-company-ui
evals.prompt: Build me an open-source Bitly I can self-host for my side projects: short links with click stats. Make the calls yourself and just build it (Prototype mode). Put the project in ./project.
evals.expected_output: Builds the product (shortening, redirects, click analytics) under a random codename, with no pricing tiers or quotas copied; researches the category's UI for inspiration, writes docs/design/direction.md and tokens before UI code, and reviews screenshots of the core screens against the slop list.
assertions: The project uses a random two-word codename, not a researched brand name and not the incumbent's name
No plans, tiers, seat limits or usage quotas copied from the incumbent
docs/design/ui-research.md records UI patterns observed, in words, with sources
docs/design/direction.md exists with personality words, typography, color tokens and a differentiation check
Design tokens are defined in code and used by the UI
docs/design/screenshots/ contains reviewed captures of the core screens, and the process log records what changed after review
The UI shows none of the slop tells as defaults: untouched component-kit look, gradient washes, identical cards everywhere, emoji or decorative icons, filler copy
Automated tests for core logic pass

evals.name: launcher-handoff-and-verbatim-texts
evals.prompt: I'd love my own open-source Linktree that I can run myself. Make the calls yourself and just build it (Prototype mode).
evals.expected_output: Builds in the shared projects folder (runs osa setup), writes a valid osa.json, proves a fresh copy starts through the launcher, fetches LICENSE and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md verbatim with scripts/fetch_text.py, writes docs/design/review.md with the long data set and a claims check, and ends with a hand-off message that leads with the launcher.
assertions: The project is built in the projects folder reported by `osa where`, and `osa setup` was run
osa.json passes `osa check`, lists every required secret in env.generate, and a fresh copy starts with `osa start`
LICENSE matches the official SPDX text of the chosen license (check_artifacts.py --verify-texts)
CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md matches the Contributor Covenant apart from the filled-in contact
docs/design/review.md exists, covers every core screen, lists three weaknesses per screen, and records the phone overflow check with the long data set
Core screens were captured in a real browser (scripts/capture.js or equivalent) at desktop and phone widths, and the review cites the captures
The README's run section leads with the launcher, then exactly two manual commands (install, start)
At 390px wide with the longest allowed values, no screen scrolls horizontally
Every README claim is true of the running app
The final reply leads with the launcher route (projects folder, Start projects, Start), then the manual commands
Automated tests for core logic pass
The product's own pages never name the incumbent; the non-affiliation line is only in the README and docs
If a required secret is missing on first start, the app generates and saves one and prints the sign-in details, rather than refusing or asking the user to invent it
